answer: Sybil resistance can be built into the registry that lets AI agents transact: each agent identity must be backed by a per-entity stake that is slashable once the same human or operator is shown to control duplicate identities, so no vault can hide a swarm behind one operator. To register, an agent posts a bond and proves control of a real funding source, and its record joins a shared grove of verified peers rather than a private nebula of clones. Anyone who reports a duplicate splits the forfeited bond, so every fake identity is a net loss, making a thousand clones cost a thousand stakes.
